what: Globe Life sells life and supplemental health insurance to working-class American families, in small policies sold face to face by its own agents and through worksite marketing.
customers: Moderate-income American households buying modest life cover and supplemental health policies.
money: small whole life and term policies
a small annuity block and investment income
moat: Captive agent networks selling in person to a market that large insurers ignore because the policies are too small to be worth their distribution costs.
risks: A short-seller report in 2024 raised allegations about agent practices and triggered regulatory interest
Recruiting and retaining agents is the growth constraint and it is persistent
opportunities: 10.3 times earnings and 8.7 times free cash flow with a 19.4% net margin
Revenue grew steadily from $5.1B to $6.0B over four years
Policies stay on the books for decades, so earnings are unusually predictable for an insurer
watch: Life premium growth and agent count.
